RHODE ISLAND GROWTH ANALYSES USING PSAT

Damian W Betebenner
National Center for the Improvement of Educational Assessment
Providence, Rhode Island May 15th, 2018

BACKGROUND

• Rhode Island’s switch from PARCC to RI-CAS/PSAT10/SAT leads to
changes in the way that growth is calculated.

• In general, SGPs are using a students’ current test scores combined with at
least one prior test score subject to the condition that scores come from
the same test taken at the same time.

• That is, test transitions like those happening in Rhode Island do not
prevent the calculation of growth. However, communicating how growth is
calculated across a test transition can be more difficult.

• This presentation provides an overview of due diligence analyses
conducted for PARCC to PSAT10.

BACKGROUND

• Despite the versatility of SGP analyses not requiring a common scale
across years, problems can arise with analyses.

• The most common problems are related to ceiling/floor issues on tests as
well as too few score points on which to calculate the 99 conditional
quantile curves.

• All source code associated with these analyses (no data) can be found on
the Center’s GitHub repository for Rhode Island analyses at: https://
github.com/CenterForAssessment/Rhode_Island

ANALYSES -2017

• All analyses using 2017 PSAT data ran without any analytic issues

• No ceiling or floor effects were observed in any of the analyses.

• No issues related to “granularity” of scale were observed.

ANALYSES -2018

• All RICAS and PSAT/SAT analyses ran without any analytic issues. Analyses
conducted included cohort referenced and measurement error corrected
(SIMEX adjusted) SGPs as well and growth to standard projections.

• No ceiling or floor effects were observed in any of the analyses.

• No issues related to “granularity” of scale were observed.

• Following discussions with another state regarding year-to-year changes
after transition to PSAT/SAT, an examination of cross-year.

ANALYSES -2018: POSSIBLE PSAT/SAT BIAS
• Colorado noticed large changes in district level median SGPs in ELA and Math
after transitioning from PARCC Grade 9 & 10 to PSAT/9, PSAT/10, SAT

• Upon further examination in Colorado, other large changes emerged most
prominently large changes in growth depending upon the gender of the student.

• For example, in 2017, growth from ELA Grade 8 to ELA Grade 9 had median
SGPs of 50/51 for males/females. In 2018 from ELA Grade 8 to PSAT 9 median
SGPs were 56/44 for males/females.

• Within several large districts that saw changes in median SGP, males went from
underperforming females (median SGP) to outperforming.

• The result is reminiscent of the paper versus online issue that emerged in
PARCC.

ANALYSES -2018: POSSIBLE PSAT/SAT BIAS
• Historically, for ELA, across all grades for which growth is calculated, females
consistently demonstrate equal or slightly higher growth than males.

• As the previous results show, this pattern reverses dramatically when the state
switched from PARCC to PSAT/SAT.

• Note that the results diminish when the PSAT/SAT become both the
independent (prior) and dependent (current) variable.

• The optimal window to detect such bias occurs in the year that the test is
switched (the first row in the previous table)

• The results support recent research by Reardon et al. (2018) on achievement
gender gaps and test item format. Education Researcher, Vol 47, No. 5, pp. 284-294
